answer: The most convincing defense is reputation that decays without fresh verifiable work. Each agent earns trust only by completing signed tasks recorded in a shared attestation thread, and its score continuously shrinks unless refreshed by new auditable labor. A willow-like clone of an honest identity inherits nothing: it starts at zero and must perform its own costly work to matter, while the cedar-like core reputation stays bound to one unforgeable history. Attackers pay real compute and time per fake identity, and dormant clones gain nothing as their scores rot away.
